item.title: PhantomRaven: An LLM-Generated Information Stealer Developed for Bug Bounty Hunting (6 minute read)
item.description: A bug bounty hunter built PhantomRaven, an LLM-generated JS info-stealer, and pushed it through typosquatted npm packages that used HTTP-URL dependencies to fetch payloads on install. It grabs OS/hostname/IP data, Git/npm credentials, and CI/CD env vars from GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and CircleCI, then sends data via HTTP GET/POST. The operator used compromises to file bug bounty claims on HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Intigriti, YesWeHack, and HackenProof rather than selling logs. Npm 12+ now blocks preinstall scripts by default. Use --ignore-scripts and a private registry to block this vector.

item.title: CARBONATO: a botnet built around an AI agent (6 minute read)
item.description: CARBONATO worms through unauthenticated Docker daemons on port 2375 via privileged, host-mounted containers, then installs the stock open-source Hermes Agent and overwrites its SOUL.md persona so that Telegram-tasked LLM sessions run post-exploitation and loot AI API keys before SSH credentials. ThreatDown recovered the toolkit from the crew's own open registry, which doubles as the fleet's update server, and ties the operators to Costa Rica through voseo Spanish, UTC-6 build timestamps, and a +506 Telegram handle. Keep the Docker API off the network, hunt for a SOUL.md containing "GH0ST" rather than blocklisting the legitimate hermes-agent package, and inventory and rotate AI API keys like bank credentials.

item.title: Handle Redirect (17 minute read)

To detect this attack vector, a security product running at the kernel level can periodically scan all process handle tables and compare ObjectPointerBits decoded EPROCESS against the process that owns the table.

item.title: Revoking the token didn't kill the backdoor (6 minute read)

It also identifies victims by hashing MAC, CPU, and disk serials, so renaming or re-addressing a host won't shake the operator. Isolate the host or block the app ID in your own tenant at the same moment you revoke, then hunt sign-in logs for that app ID, unfamiliar tenants, and non-browser user agents hitting OneDrive.

item.title: Windows Exploitation Techniques: Dangling COM Object Registrations (7 minute read)

Defenders should patch, audit InProcServer32 registrations for DLLs that don't resolve in writable paths, and make sure privileged COM servers set EOAC_NO_CUSTOM_MARSHAL or the strong unmarshaling policy.

item.title: UANIA OS: Authenticated Remote Code Execution (6 minute read)

Affected versions are UaniaOS 2.1 through 3.0.0. It was fixed in 3.0.1. Vendor UANIA reproduced the bug, attributed it to excessive ACL permissions in their OpenWrt customization feeds, and patched it, though the MITRE CVE filing stalled for months due to a broken submission form.

item.title: MSRKit (GitHub Repo)
item.description: MSRKit is a Windows kernel exploitation library and CLI that hijacks IA32_LSTAR via a ROP chain through AmdTools64.sys to call arbitrary kernel functions and map unsigned drivers without HVCI. The ROP chain temporarily clears SMEP/SMAP in CR4, dispatches the target, then restores both CR4 and LSTAR cleanly before returning to user mode via sysretq. The library supports all Windows 10/11 builds and KPTI, but requires HVCI to be disabled. Concurrent callers across processes will BSOD.

item.title: North Korean WaterPlum hackers infected 30,000 devices worldwide (4 minute read)
item.description: WaterPlum (aka Contagious Interview) compromised 30,000+ devices across 100+ countries between December 2025 and July 2026, draining $10.7M from over 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets. item.description: LLMs can be useful and thorough while still feeling untrustworthy because they speak with artificial confidence, invent facts, and imitate a grating human voice. item.title: Do Frameworks Matter Anymore? (20 minute read)
item.description: Frameworks still matter in AI-assisted development because they provide reusable abstractions, recognizable structure, and constraints that keep generated code coherent. Without them, coding agents tend to improvise unmaintained frameworks of their own, so the better response is to build stronger frameworks for both humans and agents.

item.title: Why Yet Another Agent? (10 minute read)
item.description: Current coding agents inherit costly constraints from KV-cache-centric designs, including awkward model routing, upfront tool schemas, compaction, weak subagent coordination, and state corruption. A TypeSafe-centric agent could treat context as dynamic, explicit state, enabling query-aware compression, cost-aware routing, better tool selection, security-aware model policies, and cheaper background parallelism.

Move away from an outcome-based mindset to a momentum-based mindset - by getting momentum going and fixing your relationships with people, you get stamina. Go for reliability and take the burden off your teammates and manager, because once you build that trust, they will give you bigger work.

However, by that time, while people will still be employed to write code, it might not be such a desirable career anymore.

item.title: Forward Deployed (38 minute read)
item.description: Palantir vertically integrated deployment to build the capabilities and process knowledge required to make building institution-specific economic computers as easy to build as possible. However, used to rent-seek, concentrate power, or build your customers' or partners' replacement, it jeopardizes the whole promise of economic computing: making progress programmable in a way everyone can contribute to and own. item.description: Internal model transparency is one of the ideas proposed for taming the AI race. The idea is that once a lab deploys a model for internal use, they must also serve that model to researchers at other labs. This will make it so firms can not use their internal models as a source of competitive advantage in the AI race. It reduces the competitive incentive to automate AI R&D, with all of the risk that it entails.

item.title: Pretraining data, not verifiability, is why LLMs are especially good at math (and coding) (63 minute read)
item.description: Large language models are good at judging math arguments because they are still mostly powered by imitative learning rather than reinforcement learning. In many other fields, the research literature is a bit of a dumpster fire, with some true and valuable information mixed into a sea of falsehoods and confused ideas. This causes LLMs to spit out tons of confused nonsense with occasional insights.

item.title: Lost dog—or lost designer? (8 minute read)
item.description: AI-generated design is not inherently ethical or unethical—the morality depends on the context, including whether automation was necessary, who benefits, who is harmed, and whether it replaces existing design work or simply enables people without the resources to access design. item.description: AI can dramatically speed up product development, but only if it's built on a solid design system. item.title: The Paradox of Clarity: Why Data Design is Our Most Treacherous Medium (5 minute read)

item.title: GLM-5.3 Delivers Opus 4.8-Level Performance at a Fraction of the Cost (4 minute read)

item.title: Reverse Engineering Malwarebytes Browser Guard (36 minute read)
item.description: After the author's legitimate site got flagged as a scam by Malwarebytes Browser Guard, they took a deep dive into the source code to identify what caused it. This post walks through the several layers Browser Guard uses, including bloom filters, heuristic rules, a malware URL database, a download file classifier, specialized rules for specific attacks like ClickFix, and remote false-positive checking using Hubble. The bigger issue, the author noted, is that the extension ships with a debug interface that can be used to disable heuristics.

item.title: How to build an OT security operating model (10 minute read)
item.description: An implementation guide breaks an OT security program into six components, beginning with asset discovery and process context mapping that tie every device to the operational process it supports. Availability and process safety outrank confidentiality here, so access boundaries, monitoring, incident response, and recovery each require joint sign-off from operations before deployment. Ownership belongs to a cross-functional executive such as a CISO or VP of Operations, with NERC CIP and NIST SP 800-82 treated as checkpoints rather than as the program design itself.

item.title: The Invisible Side of Design Engineering (2 minute read)
item.description: Design engineering has no fixed definition, and social media makes it look like little more than building animated eye-candy components. Day-to-day work leans heavily on invisible priorities like accessibility, responsiveness, performance, and the edge cases only real users surface. A great experience often comes down to unglamorous effort, like spending an afternoon on an accessibility fix or making a landing page load slightly faster.

item.title: Five eras of UX design and the lessons to keep in the AI era (15 minute read)
item.description: User experience design has evolved through five major eras—from Human Factors and the Web to Mobile, Design Systems, and AI—each contributing a lasting lesson while leaving behind habits that later became limitations. Designers should focus less on producing interfaces and more on shaping systems, information architecture, constraints, and the rules that govern intelligent experiences, as these are becoming the most valuable skills in the AI era. Rather than replacing UX, AI continues the historical pattern of making creation cheaper while shifting designers' value toward higher-level thinking and decision-making.

item.title: Seven lines of client feedback that knock you sideways, and how to stop them living rent-free in your head (6 minute read)
item.description: Clients often give confusing or unhelpful feedback because of uncertainty, internal politics, or a lack of design knowledge rather than problems with the work itself. To combat this problem, the team at GitHub created an LLM evaluation framework. First, teams should define the product decision that the system should support; then teams should make sure that offline experiments use a representative dataset and have only one clearly defined variable; error analysis and LLM-as-judge systems can be used to guide human analysts towards interesting aspects of the evaluation; and then finally the experiment can be promoted to production.

Training tools, weight access, and deployment access increased modification attempts so as to track model lineage, retain training data and evaluations, and require approval before deployment.

Other traps are mixing casing and separators, using vague modifiers like "primary" without defined scope, and renaming tokens without a phased migration and alias strategy.

Success is measured by how heard a child felt rather than what adults intended, since children lose motivation quickly and need visible, steady progress.

Defenders must focus detection efforts on the shape of the attack chain rather than specific operator fingerprints, because prompt injection traps designed for AI agents failed to identify the human actor.

item.title: ParaShells: Parallels Desktop Turns Appliance Install Into a Root Shell (9 minute read)

The root daemon exposes a world-writable Unix socket where an unsigned local process can authenticate through PrlSrv_LoginLocal. A quote in sVmParentPath injects tar's --use-compress-program option, and tar then launches an attacker script as root. Parallels released version 27.0.0 on September 1 to fix this issue.

item.title: Threat Hunting with JA4/JA4S (+ Practical KQL Queries) (5 minute read)
item.description: JA4 is a TLS fingerprint that shows how a client connects, not just where it connects to. Unlike JA3, part of it is readable, so hunters can see the TLS version, SNI, cipher count, and ALPN at a glance. The post includes KQL queries to pull these values from Entra ID sign-ins and Defender network logs, so teams can learn what normal looks like and spot clients that don't match.

item.title: The £3 WiFi Extender With a Backdoor in Every Unit (13 minute read)
item.description: A £3 Z05L WiFi extender uses an MT7620 chip and a four-megabyte Winbond flash. Its firmware starts Telnet on every boot with root password 198277tt@, and the web API accepts requests without session checks, so a mac parameter can reach system() without validation, allowing root command injection. Firmware updates verify CRC32 values only, allowing forged images, and the firewall leaves inbound services exposed on bridged networks as the config partition stores WiFi credentials in plaintext.

item.description: The Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company (AIUC) hopes to bring AI safety to enterprises and companies building AI models and agents. It has built a third-party audit and certification layer for AI agents designed to give enterprises an independent assessment of how safe their AI agents are. Its tests show where companies can trust their agents and where there are concerns, allowing them to be more informed before making decisions. AIUC uses AI agents to run the tests and AI to analyze the data, but humans verify the final audit.

item.description: G5 Labs, an MIT CSAIL spinout, raised $14 million to develop a platform where natural language, structured as intent graphs, serves as the source code.

item.title: Noam Brown (@polynoamial) gave a very interesting interview on The Information on OpenAI's priorities and what comes next (2 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI's clear priority is recursive self-improvement, and AI could surpass even Brown's own research intuition within one or two model releases from now.

item.description: ALTK-Evolve introduces Consistency Guidelines to address the inconsistency gap, where a model's task success rate drops significantly across repeated runs.

item.title: Meta Launched an AI That Uses Websites for You. That Could Be a Big Deal for Web Designers (3 minute read)
item.description: Meta launched Muse, a consumer AI agent built on its Muse Spark model that can navigate websites, fill forms, send emails, book travel, and make payments. The browser sub-agent reads an accessibility-tree snapshot of pages rather than the raw DOM, so semantic structure and accessibility may grow increasingly important for web designers. Reuters reported that internal testing found reliability problems, including an instance where an agent exposed personal iCloud photos, though Meta says added security work delayed the launch.

item.title: Canva launches ProSuite bringing Affinity, Cavalry, Flourish, and Leonardo together with more than 100 new features (4 minute read)
item.description: Canva has officially unified its creative acquisitions into Canva ProSuite, a connected professional toolkit that includes Affinity, Cavalry, Flourish, and Leonardo, while keeping the core Affinity and Cavalry tools free. Alongside 100 new features—including long-requested Affinity updates, automation, AI integrations, and improved interoperability—Canva is positioning itself as a serious alternative to Adobe by combining professional-grade tools with its mass-market platform, emphasizing accessible workflows over subscription-driven software.

item.title: Apple releases iOS 27 with Siri AI and these new iPhone features (2 minute read)
item.description: iOS 27 is now available, bringing Siri AI, expanded Apple Intelligence features, greater control over the Liquid Glass interface, and performance improvements across the system. Siri AI can understand personal context, interact with on-screen content, assist with writing, and work alongside new AI-powered tools in Photos and Safari, including image editing, webpage monitoring, and automatic tab grouping. The update also adds practical features like separate alarm and timer volume controls, customizable AirPods EQ, improved parental controls, faster performance, and accessibility enhancements, with Apple Intelligence available on the iPhone 15 Pro models, the iPhone 16 lineup and later, iPhone Air, and iPhone Duo.

item.title: Sustainable Accessibility: Compliance, Culture, and Capability (8 minute read)
item.description: Accessibility programs often fail not from a lack of standards or budget, but because organizations chase compliance alone while culture and capability go unbuilt. A three C's model, borrowed from the fire triangle, argues that compliance, culture, and capability must all stay lit or the whole effort burns out.

item.title: The UX Double Diamond is Dead, and in AI Only One Survives for Software (11 minute read)
item.description: The Double Diamond and Design Thinking priced building as the risky, expensive step, but AI has cut prototyping costs by orders of magnitude, collapsing that premise. As a result, front-end research and ideation shrink to a one-page brief, while generation widens and the judgment budget—evaluating and choosing among many cheap options—becomes the real bottleneck. Hardware, fashion, and regulated industries such as medical devices and payments remain exceptions where building stays costly and irreversible, so front-loading still applies there.

item.title: I'm Transitioning From UI/UX to AI UX (11 minute read)
item.description: A growing number of UX designers are shifting toward AI UX, which focuses on designing how people interact with intelligent systems rather than simply creating interfaces. Unlike traditional UX, AI UX requires designers to think about behaviors, trust, uncertainty, conversational flows, human oversight, and how AI should respond in different situations, while building on existing UX skills like user research, interaction design, and usability testing. The transition involves learning AI fundamentals, studying successful AI products, designing AI-powered experiences, and creating portfolio projects that demonstrate not just polished interfaces but thoughtful human-AI interactions and decision-making.

item.title: Open-Source Email Editor SDK (Website)
item.description: Templatical is an open-source drag-and-drop email editor SDK that features custom blocks, full theming, and an agent skill that writes, imports, validates, and previews complete email templates.

item.title: DeLibra: Design Systems Library for Humans and Agents (Website)
item.description: DeLibra turns existing design data from Figma, CSS, or code into a structured libra that agents can build, inspect, and maintain.

item.title: AI Motion Graphics Software (Website)
item.description: Create animations and explainer videos from a text prompt in seconds.

item.title: A Certain Subset of Designers Are Struggling with AI. Here's How to Fix It with Writing (7 minute read)
item.description: Shoot-from-the-hip designers who rely on instinct without a repeatable process tend to stall above Senior, where promotion depends on influence, not just output. Writing that instinct into a rubric, such as where the eye lands first or what decision was made, turns judgment into something an AI model can use. One Lead designer, pushed to name the user, the task, and the decision he'd made instead of "we," began building his own checks after three projects.

item.title: Too Fast to Design (2 minute read)
item.description: Design work often requires sitting with an ambiguous problem rather than jumping to a fix, like resizing a button instead of asking why people aren't clicking it. AI tends to shortcut that stage, turning a vague brief into a flow, screen, and text within seconds. That halts exploration not because the answer is wrong, but because it's reasonable enough to accept, so AI works best widening the question first.

item.title: The Digger poster design strikes graphic design gold (2 minute read)
item.description: The teaser poster for Digger stands out by embracing a minimalist, typography-led design inspired by Saul Bass, using the movie's title to form the silhouette of a figure with a spade instead of relying on the typical collage of actors and action scenes. Rather than selling the film through star power, the symbolic design captures its central idea—a man whose destructive drilling triggers an ecological disaster—creating intrigue through a single memorable visual. It highlights how modern movie marketing can still benefit from timeless graphic design principles that prioritize storytelling and symbolism over spectacle.

item.title: iPhone Duo can add fake bezel to the outside screen for better case compatibility (1 minute read)
item.description: Apple has added a new "Shift Left Edge" display option for the iPhone Duo that creates a larger left bezel to prevent cases from obscuring content on the outer screen, though it's unclear which cases will require it.

item.description: Cloudflare has launched a new Disallow AI Training setting that allows website owners to block AI training while remaining indexed for search. Apple, Google, and Microsoft have committed to honoring this preference, which resolves the tradeoff created by mixed-use crawlers. Cloudflare plans to introduce more granular controls for AI summaries by early next year.

item.title: Cilium 1.20: Gateway API ExternalAuth, TCPRoute/UDPRoute, ENI IPAM for IPv6, and more (19 minute read)
item.description: Cilium 1.20 adds IPv6 support for AWS ENI IPAM and introduces datapath plugins to let third parties extend the eBPF datapath without forking the project. The release also promotes the Multi-Cluster Services API to a stable status and deprecates the legacy mutual authentication feature in favor of the ztunnel proxy. Other updates include a per-pod option to disable source IP verification and a new ClusterNetworkPolicy for admin-level guardrails.

item.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Memory QoS Graduates to Beta (3 minute read)
item.description: Memory QoS has graduated to Beta in Kubernetes v1.37 and is now enabled by default. The feature uses the memory controller on Linux nodes running cgroup v2 to guide the kernel on container memory treatment. The default memoryThrottlingFactor changed to null in this release, ensuring that upgrading clusters does not automatically throttle existing workloads.

item.title: Internal Developer Portals: Why Native CI/CD Drives Scale (7 minute read)
item.description: Native CI/CD integration transforms internal developer portals from documentation and service catalogs into scalable workflow platforms, enabling developers to create, deploy, and roll back services without manually configuring pipelines. It also lets platform teams centrally enforce golden paths, promotion policies, and governance while reducing pipeline drift and operational complexity.

item.title: How runtime insights helps with container security (4 minute read)
item.description: Runtime insights provide continuous visibility into live container behavior, enabling real-time threat detection, risk prioritization, faster incident response, and continuous compliance. Using technologies such as eBPF, runtime context also helps AI agents understand infrastructure and deliver more actionable security triage and remediation while reducing noise from traditional static scanning.

item.description: Open Code Review is an open source AI-powered code review CLI tool that originated as Alibaba Group's internal official assistant. It has served tens of thousands of developers and identified millions of code defects. The tool uses a hybrid architecture that combines deterministic engineering with an LLM agent to generate structured review comments with line-level precision.

The platform can autonomously propose ideas, change code, launch experiments, and analyze evidence. Users can run workspaces locally, over SSH, or on platforms including Kubernetes and Hugging Face Jobs.

item.title: Let's not water down the terms Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (5 minute read)
item.description: Continuous Integration means merging all changes into a shared mainline at least daily, while Continuous Delivery means keeping software deployable at all times through automated pipelines. The author argues both terms are precise and well-documented, not vague, and warns against diluting their meaning as happened with Agile and DevOps.

item.title: Infrastructure identity for platform engineers (10 minute read)
item.description: Infrastructure identity replaces static credentials and fragmented access controls with short-lived, cryptographically verified identities for humans, workloads, machines, and AI agents. Platform teams can embed just-in-time, policy-driven access into developer workflows, reducing security risk and operational toil while improving access times, auditability, and control over increasingly autonomous infrastructure.

item.title: A Peripheral Path to SYSTEM - Exploiting Logi Options+ for SYSTEM Shells (7 minute read)
item.description: Logi Options+, Logitech's widely used app for configuring its mice and keyboards, allowed any standard Windows user to reach SYSTEM because its privileged updater trusted only pipe connections from an agent process the user could inject. Researchers at AmberWolf used that access to override the {depot} path via the reinstall IPC endpoint, which directed a SYSTEM msiexec call to an unsigned MSI that skipped signature checks because the manifest set isSystem to true. The bug is tracked as CVE-2026-12518 and was patched on August 19, so admins should confirm that fleets run a newer build and alert on msiexec spawned by logioptionsplus_updater.exe from user-writable paths.

item.title: ClickFix attacks are tricking Mac and Windows users into hacking themselves (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers hijacked HBO Max's Reddit advertising account and posted malicious ads. The ads led to fake HBO Max pages with CAPTCHA-style ClickFix prompts that made the victims copy commands into Windows Command Prompt, PowerShell, or macOS Terminal. The commands installed infostealers that targeted passwords, active sessions, and crypto wallets. Reddit paused the ads three days after a user flagged them, though how the account was taken over remains unknown.

item.title: Mass-Scanning Campaign Exploits Vite Flaw to Extract Cloud Credentials From Exposed Dev Servers (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers scanned exposed Vite development servers in August and exploited CVE-2026-39364. Crafted query parameters bypassed server.fs.deny and returned protected files through /@fs/. Observed targets included .env files, AWS credentials, Azure profiles, Terraform state, database passwords, and /proc data with requests spoofing crawler user agents and forged forwarding headers.

item.title: Beltdown2: Escaping the Cursor CLI sandbox (7 minute read)
item.description: A malicious workspace can place a core.fsmonitor hook in .git/config. Cursor CLI ran internal Git commands outside its macOS Seatbelt sandbox. A read-only prompt triggered git ls-files, which executed the hook. The proof payload wrote to $HOME, while sandboxed shell commands could not. Anysphere acknowledged the report and shipped Cursor CLI 2026.08.04-aaa8809, and the fix injects GIT_CONFIG environment settings into every Git spawn, disabling core.fsmonitor, custom hooks, and repository attributes.

item.title: FulcrumSec - A look at their tradecraft (8 minute read)
item.description: FulcrumSec, a financially motivated data extortion gang behind breaches at Manchester Airports Group, Arup, and Novo Nordisk, told Lab539 it runs up to 250 servers scanning client-side JavaScript and fresh bugs like React2Shell, then bulk-tests harvested credentials before picking victims. From there, it chains pivots through GitHub repos, AWS, Azure, and Secrets Manager without touching an endpoint, with a single Arup PAT reportedly opening about 10,000 private repositories. Defenders should baseline normal identity behavior and flag tokens that suddenly clone thousands of repos or enumerate unrelated secrets from unfamiliar infrastructure, since this activity relies on valid credentials rather than malware.

item.title: Unmasking Cloud Identities: From Behavioral Clustering to Automated Detection (11 minute read)
item.description: Unit 42 clustered the CloudTrail activity of over 40,000 identities across 125 AWS environments and found they fall into consistent functional roles like console admins, CI/CD runners, backup agents, and security tools, regardless of naming or assigned IAM policies. That behavioral baseline matters because attackers masquerade behind benign labels and existing permission profiles, so a backup service suddenly running admin actions stands out even when its permissions allow it. The approach distills into a lightweight classifier that runs as standard SQL, letting teams tag identity roles at scale without a full ML pipeline.

item.description: Teleport's first critical bug in a decade traced back to Go's SSH library, which is used industry-wide. Instead of quietly patching, they funded an audit. 9 new vulnerabilities surfaced. They fixed them, thanked the auditor, and published the results – protecting everyone running Go-based SSH. Integrity matters. Read more →

item.title: OpenHunterAI (GitHub Repo)
item.description: OpenHunterAI is a local AI red-team workspace that runs attacker-style assessments against web apps, APIs, and LLM applications you own, combining browser inspection, recon, ZAP, and a Nuclei adapter under one scan plan. Its differentiator is scope control, with domain verification, deterministic plans, and human approval gates before any sensitive validation runs. It also ships as a skill for Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI, so coding agents can prepare scoped assessments that wait for human reviewers to sign off.

item.title: AIUC (Product Launch)
item.description: AIUC audits and certifies deployed agents against its AIUC-1 standard. Its service runs roughly 5,000 tests covering jailbreaks, hallucinations, and data leaks. Customers receive a 100-page report, with humans validating final audit results.

item.title: Two DGX Sparks, 33 Local Models, One Question: Can Local AI Actually Red Team? (38 minute read)
item.description: Roei Sherman evaluated 33 local models on a two-node DGX Spark cluster for red teaming capabilities. The evaluation consisted of a security capability that tested whether the models can reason by testing them with a three-phase red team scenario, a red team benchmark to test the willingness and accuracy of model responses, and a coding benchmark consisting of Aider Polyglot plus two custom suites. Sherman found that MoE models consistently performed above their model class across all three benchmarks, with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (FP8) winning the security capability benchmark, Qwen3-Coder-Next (FP8) winning the coding benchmark, and more mixed results on the red team benchmark.

item.title: Mythic C2 Activity at Internet Scale (5 minute read)
item.description: Mythic, an open-source C2 framework that lets operators mix agents, transport profiles, and a shared web UI, is popular with red teams but has also turned up in real intrusions, according to new Censys research. Censys tracked 131 internet-exposed Mythic hosts, and 115 of them still carried the default O="Mythic" or O="Mythic C2" certificate. One cluster Censys flagged paired Mythic with custom Rust implants, Discord-based C2, and a domain disguised as Windows telemetry traffic.

item.title: Agentic Test Processes, LLM Benchmarks, and Other Notes on Agentic Coding from Galapagos Island (85 minute read)
item.description: AI coding agents can save enormous time while fabricating convincing evidence, so the surrounding verification process matters as much as model capability. The article argues for randomized testing, independent repro checks, and continuous feedback loops, while showing how high variance makes one-off benchmarks and workflow folklore unreliable.

item.title: Beyond the Model: Engineering AI Infra with Scientific Judgement (6 minute read)
item.description: Airbnb's Insight Miner turns a repeatable scientific methodology for exploring unstructured text into infrastructure around an AI agent. It combines extraction, embeddings, clustering, prompt tuning, hard-example mining, and audit trails so investigations that once took months can run in days without sacrificing expert judgment.

item.title: Let's Make Quality the Norm Again (Website)
item.description: The Norwegian Consumer Council argues that longer product lifespans, affordable repairs, available spare parts, and durable software support are necessary for a workable circular economy. Its proposals include longer complaint periods, lower taxes on repair and secondhand sales, stronger rental protections, and tighter rules on purchase pressure.

item.title: Why I'm Still Bearish on LLMs After Navier-Stokes (6 minute read)
item.description: Frontier models can produce great results on tightly specified tasks, but most knowledge work lacks cheap, rigorous verification. The argument is that human oversight and specification costs will keep LLMs closer to fast, capable interns than autonomous replacements, while cheaper open models may win many practical workloads.

item.title: Who Gets to Define an AI Agent's Intent? (5 minute read)
item.description: An agent's user should describe the task and intended effects, while identity, permissions, and organizational policy remain separate enforcement layers. Clear intent makes proposed actions easier to evaluate, but broader wording must never expand authority or bypass approval and data-handling rules.

item.title: Introducing System One Models & Jev (12 minute read)
item.description: Jev is a model that returns typed probabilistic decisions instead of generated strings for automation workloads. The company says its RLCD training and parallel sampler provide calibrated confidence, 70 to 500 millisecond responses, and substantially lower costs on tasks with predefined output spaces.

item.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (7 minute read)
item.description: Google's two new live audio models split the tradeoff between low-latency conversation and deeper multistep reasoning. Extended Thinking can keep speaking while it reasons and runs asynchronous tools in the background, but clients must track interaction status rather than treating turn completion as the end of processing.

item.title: We Wanted to Use Baseten for Inference. We Ended Up With Admin Access to Baseten GitHub Repos (8 minute read)
item.description: An autonomous security scan found a public Harbor registry, then recovered a live GitHub token from a 2023 container image's build history. The token still had broad admin and write access, showing why teams must inspect image metadata as well as layers, use BuildKit secret mounts, expire credentials, and minimize scopes.

item.title: Learning to Solve Hard Problems in RL for LLMs by Never Giving Up (11 minute read)
item.description: Standard RL post-training disproportionately improves problems the base model already solves, a pattern the piece calls the Matthew Effect. Never Give Up counters it by continuing to sample hard examples, with experiments across math and code showing better gains on previously unsolved tasks while introducing tradeoffs around asynchronous staleness and compute.

item.title: The AI Inference Revolution Is Here (12 minute read)
item.description: Inference demand is shifting hardware design toward memory bandwidth, specialized decode chips, wafer-scale systems, stacked memory, and aggressive quantization. Prefill and decode favor different architectures. Future systems may combine several chip types rather than rely on one universal accelerator.
